title: Sleepless in Seattle
tagline: Meet me at the top of the Empire State.
about: A widower's son calls a radio show and a woman across the country falls for his dad.
cue: Serve dessert when Jonah calls the late-night radio show on Christmas Eve.
faces: The view from our window tables on Valentine’s night.
Hot-smoked fish worked into cream cheese and crème fraîche with dill, capers, lemon and horseradish. Toasted bagel chips.
Maryland lump meat, barely bound and pan browned, with remoulade.
Five on crushed ice with cocktail sauce and a wedge of lemon.
Dinner from six. Dancing until one.
Fillet roasted under parsley, grated lemon peel and bread crumbs. Steamed green beans, warm butter spooned over.
Ten ounces, grilled to order, with béarnaise and potatoes Anna.
Rosemary and garlic, with wild rice.
Browned butter sugar cookies, hand cut, iced red and white.
A pair on every saucer tonight.
Dark chocolate, baked to order, sauce poured at the table.
Strong coffee with dark chocolate melted through, cold milk over ice, whipped cream and cocoa.
The way they take it in Seattle.
Popped in coconut oil, tossed with browned butter and sea salt.
Bar radio stays on the call-in show.
Candles and roses on every table, February 14.
Two at eight, by the window. Please tell the kitchen about my allergies. Something mild.

Toasted bagel chips.Flown in overnight from Seattle.How to make it200g hot-smoked salmon150g cream cheese100ml crème fraîche1 lemon, juiced2 tbsp chopped dill1 tbsp capers1 tsp horseradish2 bagels1 tbsp oilFlake the salmon into the cream cheese and crème fraîche.Add lemon juice, dill, capers and horseradish and mix.Slice the bagels thin and brush with oil.Bake at 180°C into crisp chips.Serve the chips with the dip.Late show popcornPopped in coconut oil, tossed with browned butter and sea salt.Bar radio stays on the call-in show.How to make it60g butter2 tbsp coconut oil120g popcorn kernels1 tsp flaky sea saltCook the butter until nutty and golden.Heat the coconut oil with 3 kernels in a lidded pot.Add the rest of the kernels once they pop, cover and shake until popping slows.Toss with the brown butter and flaky salt.MainsBaked salmonFillet roasted under parsley, grated lemon peel and bread crumbs. Steamed green beans, warm butter spooned over.Mild. Nothing to sneeze at.How to make it50g panko breadcrumbs1 handful parsley, chopped2 lemons, 1 zested, 1 juiced, 1 in wedges2 tbsp oil4 salmon fillets300g green beans60g butterMix the panko with parsley, lemon zest and oil.Press onto the salmon and roast at 200°C.Steam the beans.Melt the butter with the lemon juice and spoon over everything.SweetsValentine heartsBrowned butter sugar cookies, hand cut, iced red and white.A pair on every saucer tonight.How to make it125g butter100g caster sugar2 eggs, 1 whole and 1 white250g plain flour300g icing sugar1 drop red food colouringBrown the butter and cool.Beat with the sugar and whole egg, then mix in the flour.Roll to 5mm and cut into hearts.Bake at 180°C.Cool completely.Mix the icing sugar with the egg white. Tint half red and ice the cookies.DrinksIced mochaStrong coffee with dark chocolate melted through, cold milk over ice, whipped cream and cocoa.The way they take it in Seattle.How to make it400ml strong brewed coffee80g dark chocolate, chopped2 tbsp sugar600ml cold milk150ml thickened cream1 tbsp cocoa powder1 bag iceStir the hot coffee with the chocolate and sugar until melted.Cool.Whip the cream.Fill 4 glasses with ice and add the mocha and milk.Top with whipped cream and dust with cocoa.
